acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Harpies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Talon, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Hook-and-Carry Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Full brown plumage, hooked talons, bone-bead necklaces, and broad wings held wide replace the Screecher's patchy molt.
Signature mechanic: Cliff Hook: the Talon plants one hooked claw, spreads full brown wings, and rakes the other claw through a fixed carry line.
battlefieldDuty: Repeat reliable aerial pressure by hooking a target toward an exposed cliff lane and releasing before a second pass.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe attachments: T1–T3 tension slotted feathers and hollow whistle bones with rawhide straps between talons and wing roots; T4–T5 anchor those cords to gold ankle rings and gold cuffs while retaining the same wing anatomy.
Airflow becomes supernatural and directional: visible compression bands follow the selected wing camber, loose feathers align into one lane, and a readable still pocket forms at the inner wing root.
counterplay: Cross behind the planted leg or strike it before launch; a missed hook forces both wings low during recovery. Affinity signal: T1–T3 pull one rawhide wing-root strap taut as loose feathers snap into a straight lane; T4–T5 lift the linked gold ankle ring or gold cuff, and every tier leaves a still inner wing root open from the lee.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only pale plumage without vane, slot, and pressure construction
Glow-only wind treatment without directional compression and a still center
Ordinary family-native flight or loose feathers presented alone as Wind affinity
Omnidirectional gust clutter that erases the attack lane
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso remains joined to large raptor wings that replace or extend the arms, backward-jointed bird legs, oversized talons, and a feathered head crest.
Slate gray, brown, and dirty cream mature into iridescent blue-green, storm purple, and white without losing the family feather pattern.
Feather, hollow bone, sinew, raw hide, braided hair, and gold ankle ornaments remain physically readable materials.
Bone jewelry, trophy feathers, braided hair, ankle rings, and crest height communicate status without changing the core wing-and-talon silhouette.
Every attack keeps the wing roots, talons, crest, and flight direction visible enough to preserve counterplay.
telegraph: Bone beads pull taut, one talon closes on stone, and the opposite leg extends beneath fully spread wings.
